You're overpaying 5× on half your Claude prompts.

Pick the wrong model and you'll burn through your usage limits much faster.

✦ Haiku 4.5

Cost: 1×
Context: 200K tokens

✅ Fastest and cheapest model.
❌ No effort dial, and its knowledge stops at February 2025.

Best for:

Summarising documents

Reformatting content

Bulk processing

Simple tasks where deep reasoning isn't needed

✦ Sonnet 5

Cost: 3×
Context: 1M tokens

✅ Best value for most users. Uses your limits the most efficiently.
❌ The hardest 10% of problems still require a larger model.

Best for:

Everyday writing

Rewrites

Drafting content

Turning notes into structured plans

✦ Opus 5

Cost: 5×
Context: 1M tokens

✅ Anthropic recommends starting here if you're unsure.
❌ Slower and consumes limits much faster.

Best for:

Strategy

Contracts

Multi-step reasoning

High-stakes work where accuracy matters

✦ Fable 5

Cost: 10×
Context: 1M tokens

✅ Can plan, build, and test its own work.
❌ Costs twice as much as Opus for similar quality.

Best for:

Long-running agentic workflows

Autonomous coding tasks

Projects you leave running for hours

Anthropic notes that Fable on Low effort often outperforms older models running on Extra effort.

Understanding the Effort Dial

Every model except Haiku includes an Effort Dial with five levels:

Low

Medium

High (Default)

Extra

Max

Here's where the best value is:

1. High ⭐
The sweet spot. Anthropic describes it as the best balance between quality and token efficiency.

2. Medium
The cost-saving option. On Sonnet 5, Medium performs similarly to Sonnet 4.6 running on High.

3. Low
Ideal for:

Bulk processing

Classification

Quick lookups

Simple automation

4. Extra
Designed for long-running agentic tasks lasting 30+ minutes.

5. Max
Generally not worth it. Anthropic says it significantly increases cost for relatively small quality improvements.

Quick Recommendations

Use caseModelEffort

Summaries & formattingHaiku 4.5—
Daily workSonnet 5High
Deep reasoningOpus 5High
Long autonomous agentsFable 5Extra

Rule of thumb

Start with Sonnet 5 (High) for most work.

Use Opus 5 (High) when accuracy is critical.

Switch to Fable 5 only for long-running autonomous workflows.

Use Haiku 4.5 whenever speed and low cost matter more than deep reasoning.

Move the effort dial before switching to a bigger model. It usually gives you a better cost-to-performance improvement.

title: Global AI Patent Grants Top 100,000 for First Time as Agentic AI Filings Accelerate
content: On Tuesday, IFI CLAIMS Patent Services released its annual report on artificial intelligence patenting, IFI Insights: Inventing AI. According to the report, worldwide AI patent grants reached 107,279 in 2025, marking the first time the total has surpassed 100,000 in a single year. The figure also represents an 83% increase over the past three years. Globally, AI patent applications reached 209,518 in 2025, of which 23% related to generative AI and 9% related to agentic AI, which is up from 5% in IFI’s previous study. title: UN chief of human rights warns Israeli strikes in Lebanon may constitute international crimes
content: UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk on Monday expressed concerns that the mass destruction and displacement caused by Israeli strikes against Lebanon could amount to international crimes. Türk spent two days in Lebanon documenting the effects of the regional war on Lebanese citizens and concluded the trip with a press conference detailing his findings. While in Lebanon, he met with individuals fleeing the conflict , many of whom conveyed that their homes, schools, healthcare facilities, electricity and water infrastructure, and agricultural land had been destroyed by Israeli strikes. “I am struck by the widespread damage and compounded suffering that I have seen,” said Türk. “The trauma, frustration, and despair are palpable- but so too is the demand for justice which I heard resoundingly.” Violence in this region is not a new concept, as conflict in Lebanon between Iranian-backed group Hezbollah and Israel has been occurring for decades . Fighting subsided in 2024 due to a ceasefire agreement between the two parties, but resumed in March of 2026 when US-Israeli airstrikes killed Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. In this latest stint of combat , more than 4,300 civilians have been killed, hundreds of thousands have fled their homes, and the Lebanese government has faced delayed elections and economic collapse. Türk indicated that this conduct may amount to violations of international humanitarian law (IHL), citing that these violations involve the failure to uphold core principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution. Indiscriminate and disproportionate attacks by Israeli military forces alongside the usage of white phosphorus munitions have been condemned by rights groups. Grave violations of IHL that amount to war crimes , such as willful killing and targeted attacks on civilians, are prosecuted by the International Criminal Court (ICC). title: Artists are lawyering up against AI slop, and some are even winning
content: Artists whose work has been co-opted by AI are taking to court. | Image: Alex Parkin / The Verge When The Atlantic published a searchable dataset of works used to train AI, Kirk Wallace Johnson, like a lot of artists, looked for his name out of curiosity. And, like a lot of artists, he found it. Essentially, his books, like The Feather Thief and The Fishermen and the Dragon - nonfiction tomes that he spent "five to six years researching, writing, and investigating" - had been pirated and fed to a chatbot.
